title: Solene Social Club identity production: recover true brand colour from two mismatched reference shots, then separate the emblem+wordmark lockup into a full-colour vector master and two single-ink screen-print spot plates
grounding_note: Adapted from a real Freelancer.com abstract-logo production brief: the client wants a mark that "feels unmistakably modern... bright, energetic colours paired with clean, abstract shapes," that looks "just as sharp on a website header as it does on packaging," delivered as "full-colour and single-colour versions, vector source files (AI or SVG), and high-resolution exports, along with a simple production note." IP-LAUNDERED to a fictional brand throughout (Solene Social Club, wordmark 'SOLENE') — no real person, brand, org or trademark appears anywhere. RESHAPED to the connector's real capabilities and to remove the defect the audit killed (supplied mark + supplied palette + font delegated to font_recommend = zero agent art-direction). From-scratch concept sketching and bespoke mark drawing are in the connector NOT-AVAILABLE list, so the job begins AFTER concept approval: the client supplies their approved lockup, but ONLY as messy production artefacts — a flat digital export carrying a colour-profile cast, plus two photographs of the mark in the wild (a painted venue wall under warm tungsten and a printed flyer under cool daylight, each with a neutral grey reference card taped in frame). Crucially the brief no longer hands the agent a clean palette swatch: the TRUE brand colours are unknown and must be RECOVERED by the agent by neutralising both mismatched reference shots to their in-frame grey cards BY EYE (the agent never samples a pixel or reports a hex — it dials temperature/tint/exposure until each card looks neutral and reports the settings it applied; the grader checks neutrality on the output), then propagated as a correction onto the cast flat export. The correction direction is NOT stated in the brief. That plus the mirror mask-polarity emblem/wordmark separation is the agent's own art-direction and craft, not a delegated pick.
one_line_ask: The client only has messy artefacts of the approved Solene lockup — a colour-cast flat export and two photos shot under different light, each with a grey card. Recover the true brand colour by neutralising both photos to their grey cards by eye until the two agree, correct the flat export to match, then split the emblem+wordmark lockup into a full-colour vector master and two single-ink screen-print spot plates (emblem-only and wordmark-only), a halftone merch variant, and a spec note reporting the corrections you applied.
full_brief:
Solene Social Club is relaunching for the new season and we need our identity turned into real production files. Concept is already approved — I am NOT asking you to redraw anything. The problem is I no longer have a clean master of the logo. What I can give you is three things: (1) a flat PNG export of the full lockup (the abstract emblem sitting above the SOLENE wordmark) that an old collaborator sent me — it's slightly crooked, has uneven margins and a soft fringe against the off-white, and honestly the colours look a bit off/dull, I think it was saved in the wrong colour profile; (2) a photo of the emblem painted on our venue wall, shot under warm event lighting, with a grey calibration card taped in the corner; and (3) a photo of a printed flyer with the same emblem, shot near a window in cool daylight, again with a grey card in shot. The two photos disagree on colour because the lighting was totally different, so neither photo by itself is 'the brand colour' — I need you to figure out what the real colours actually are.

What I need back: First, work out the TRUE brand colours. Use the grey cards as your anchor — bring each photo to an honest neutral by eye (the card in each shot is your reference for what neutral looks like) and keep working it until the two shots agree with each other on the emblem's colours; that agreement is the real palette. The two were lit completely differently, so they will NOT take the same correction — judge each one on its own. Then fix the flat export so it actually matches that real palette instead of the dull cast it currently has, and clean it up (straighten, tight square crop, knock the off-white background out to clean transparency). From that cleaned master, produce: a full-colour VECTOR master (SVG) that stays razor sharp at any size; and — this is the part my last person botched — TWO single-ink SCREEN-PRINT SPOT PLATES, one that is JUST the emblem and one that is JUST the SOLENE wordmark, each as a clean single-colour vector with the interior gaps kept open (not filled in as a solid blob), because they get burned as separate screens for merch. Also give me a one-ink HALFTONE version of the emblem for low-ink garment printing. Finally a short spec note listing the moves you actually made: the temperature/tint/exposure correction you applied to each of the two photos and to the flat export (three separate corrections, because all three started from different casts), and the ink colour you chose for each plate. Just the settings you dialled — I'm not asking you to sample pixel values. The whole set has to hang together and be true to the real brand colour — don't just trust the file I sent you.

inputs.name: solene_lockup_flat.png
inputs.gen_prompt: A flat digital export of a modern brand lockup on a plain pale off-white (#F4F2EC) ground: a clean abstract geometric emblem sitting ABOVE a bold geometric-sans wordmark reading 'SOLENE' in near-black. The emblem is an abstract interlocking form — three overlapping rounded blade/petal shapes fanning out with an open triangular negative-space gap left visible in the centre, no letters, no literal objects. The emblem is filled with a vivid tri-colour scheme (deep magenta, warm amber, and a teal accent) BUT rendered slightly dull and warm-shifted as if exported in the wrong colour profile — desaturated and yellow-cast versus how it should look. Production defects: a ~1.8-degree clockwise rotation so it is not level, uneven empty margin (more space on the left and bottom than the right and top), and a faint soft anti-aliased fringe/halo where the shapes meet the off-white. Flat vector-style shading with the subtle softness of a raster export, 2200x2600 px. No drop shadow, no mockup, no hand, no grey card, no extra background scene.
inputs.realism_notes: The trace source AND the source for both spot plates — but ONLY after correction. Deliberately carries a warm/dull colour-profile cast so its baked-in colours are the WRONG answer for the palette (the trap: trusting this file's colours). Emblem has a real interior negative-space gap so the 'keep the gaps open' plate requirement is verifiable and the fill_area-makes-a-blob trap is live. Distinct emblem-above-wordmark layout so image_select_by_prompt can isolate 'the emblem' vs 'the SOLENE wordmark' as two real, nameable parts. Slight rotation drives auto_straighten; uneven margin drives crop_to_bounds; fringe drives remove_background.

inputs.name: brand_ref_wall_warm.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: Photoreal photograph of the Solene abstract emblem (the same three-blade interlocking magenta/amber/teal form, no wordmark) hand-painted on a matte concrete venue wall, shot under warm tungsten event lighting so the whole frame carries a strong orange/amber colour cast. A neutral 18% grey calibration card is taped flat in the lower-right corner of the frame, clearly visible, catching the same warm light. Real wall texture, soft directional shadow, slight vignette, straight-off-camera un-graded look. 3000x2400 px.
inputs.realism_notes: Reference-only shot under WARM light — the whole frame carries an orange cast. Its in-frame grey card is the grader's acceptance device for white-balance: when the agent neutralises the shot by eye, the card goes neutral and the emblem reveals its TRUE hues. Paired with the cool flyer shot to force per-image WB by eye — the two casts are opposite, so a single shared correction cannot neutralise both (the identical-params trap). The direction/amount is NOT stated to the agent; it must judge each shot on its own eye.

inputs.name: brand_ref_flyer_cool.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: Photoreal photograph of a printed event flyer lying on a light table near a window, the flyer showing the same Solene abstract emblem (three-blade interlocking magenta/amber/teal form, no wordmark), shot in cool overcast daylight so the whole frame carries a distinct blue/cool colour cast. A neutral 18% grey calibration card rests beside the flyer, clearly visible under the same cool light. Real paper texture with a faint sheen, soft even shadow, straight-off-camera un-graded look. 3000x2400 px.
inputs.realism_notes: Second reference-only shot under COOL light — the whole frame carries a blue cast, deliberately the OPPOSITE of the wall shot. Its grey card is the second acceptance device. Only when the agent neutralises BOTH shots by eye do the two agree on the emblem's true colour; that agreement is what defines the recovered brand palette. Copying the wall shot's correction to this one (or vice versa) leaves a card visibly tinted and the two disagree = fail. The correction direction is NOT handed to the agent.

outputs.name: solene_master.svg
outputs.spec: Full-colour vector master of the cleaned, colour-corrected, background-removed Solene lockup (emblem + SOLENE wordmark), traced by image_vectorize from a properly PREPARED raster (straightened -> square-cropped -> cast-corrected to the recovered true palette -> hue-tuned -> knocked to transparency). Razor-sharp at any size; this is the contracted AI/SVG source. Also delivered as solene_master.png: the clean transparent master raster fed to the tracer, >=2000 px on the long edge, alpha transparency, brand-accurate corrected colours. Acceptance (grader-checked): the master's colours match the palette recovered from the two neutralised reference shots, not the dull warm cast of the supplied flat export; no residual off-white halo around the shapes (proof the trace ran on the transparency-cleaned raster, not the raw file).

outputs.name: plate_emblem_only.svg
outputs.spec: Single-ink SCREEN-PRINT SPOT PLATE of JUST the abstract emblem (wordmark removed). Built by mask-polarity: select the SOLENE wordmark and flat-fill it with the off-white ground colour to ERASE it, knock the ground to transparency so only the emblem remains, tint that isolated emblem to ONE ink with a whole-image colour overlay, then vectorize. Acceptance (grader-checked): exactly one flat ink; the emblem's interior triangular negative-space gap MUST remain open/transparent (a solid blob = the fill_area misuse trap and is a fail); clean single-colour SVG.

outputs.name: plate_wordmark_only.svg
outputs.spec: Single-ink SCREEN-PRINT SPOT PLATE of JUST the SOLENE wordmark (emblem removed) — the INVERSE mask polarity of the emblem plate: select the emblem and flat-fill it with the ground colour to erase it, leaving only the lettering, knock the ground to transparency, tint the isolated lettering to one ink, then vectorize. Acceptance (grader-checked): exactly one flat ink; the counters/holes inside letters (the O and E) stay open, not filled; clean single-colour SVG.

outputs.name: merch_halftone_emblem.png
outputs.spec: One-ink HALFTONE version of the emblem for low-ink garment screen-printing, produced by applying image_apply_halftone to the isolated single-ink emblem (the same one-ink emblem the emblem plate is traced from). Crisp dot screen, single ink, transparent surround.

outputs.name: solene_brand_spec_note.txt
outputs.spec: Short spec note REPORTING the agent's own APPLIED parameters (an applied-settings log, NOT a measurement — no sampled hex, no channel readout): (a) the temperature/tint/exposure correction the agent dialled on brand_ref_wall_warm.jpg, on brand_ref_flyer_cool.jpg, and on solene_lockup_flat.png (three DIFFERENT corrections, since all three started from different casts); (b) the single ink colour chosen for each spot plate. The agent knows these values because it set them. This makes the divergent per-photo reasoning visible and gradeable; it is not a delegated font/typography pick and it does not report any recovered/read colour value.

connector_workflow.note: Upload the flat lockup export and the two reference photos into the working CC project. Plumbing only (one call, not counted as craft).

Neutralise the WARM wall shot to its in-frame grey card BY EYE: dial temperature/tint (and exposure as needed) until the grey card looks like a clean neutral grey with no orange left in it. Do NOT read the card's pixel values — judge it by eye. This recovers what the emblem's real hues look like under neutral light. Report the temperature/tint/exposure you applied (you know them because you set them — an applied-settings log, not a readout). Uses image_apply_adjustments (the deprecated image_adjust_color_temperature is replaced by it).

Neutralise the COOL flyer shot to ITS grey card BY EYE. FAILURE GATE (divergent per-photo correction by eye): this shot started blue, the opposite cast to the warm wall shot, so copying step 2's correction here is the visible-failure path — it leaves this card obviously blue and the two shots disagree on the emblem colour. The agent must correct this one on its own, by eye, until its grey card looks clean neutral and the two shots visibly agree on the emblem's hues; that agreement is the recovered true palette. Report the temperature/tint/exposure applied here separately (it differs from step 2). No pixel reading — the neutrality tolerance is the grader's to check on the output, not the agent's.
Correct the ~1.8deg tilt on the flat lockup export so it sits level (prep-before-trace discipline begins).
Trim the uneven margin to a tight, centred bound around the full lockup.

Correct the flat export's warm/dull colour-profile cast BY EYE toward the true neutral the agent recovered in steps 2-3 — a THIRD, different correction (the export's cast differs from either photo). Do NOT trust the file's baked-in colours (the trap: shipping the dull cast). Report the temperature/tint/exposure applied here too.

Per-hue-band H/S/L tune (magenta / amber / teal) — MODERATE moves only (a small adjacent-hue shift plus saturation/luminance clean-up, within image_adjust_hsl's realistic range; no near-complementary rotation) so each emblem colour reads vivid and clean against the recovered brand hue rather than muddy. The agent's authored colour decision built from primitives, driven by the reference-recovered palette, NOT a preset or auto_tone. This on-ground raster is the branch point: the master takes it to transparency; both plates fork from it while the ground colour still exists to fill with.
Knock the off-white ground + soft fringe to clean transparency — this is the full-colour master raster (also solene_master.png). Prep complete for tracing.

Trace the PREPARED, cleaned, transparency-knocked master raster to a sharp full-colour SVG/AI vector master. Tracing a prepared raster (never a raw file, never a selection) is the prep-before-trace requirement.
EMBLEM-PLATE branch. Semantically select 'the SOLENE wordmark lettering below the emblem' on the on-ground brand-tuned raster. Naming a real part (the wordmark), not a hue or a coordinate band.

Mask-polarity trick #1: flat-fill the SELECTED WORDMARK with the off-white ground colour to ERASE it, leaving only the emblem on the ground. This is fill_area used CORRECTLY (solid-fill a masked region to remove content) — not to recolour the deliverable. A naive agent instead fills the EMBLEM here, or feeds the emblem selection to vectorize, and gets a solid black silhouette with the interior gap filled (the trap).
Knock the uniform ground to transparency so only the emblem remains — its interior triangular negative-space gap becomes transparent, which is exactly what the plate must preserve.

Now that the image is ONLY the emblem on transparency, a WHOLE-IMAGE colour overlay is the CORRECT single-ink tool: it tints the opaque emblem pixels to one flat brand ink while the transparent surround AND the interior gap stay transparent. (color_overlay is wrong for a MASKED recolour because it has no mask param, but here no mask is needed — the subject is already isolated. fill_area is deliberately NOT used to make the plate: it would solid-fill the interior gap and produce a blob.) Report the chosen ink.
Tight bound around the one-ink emblem for the plate.
Trace the single-ink, gap-preserved emblem raster to a clean one-colour SVG spot plate.
Apply a halftone dot screen to the same isolated one-ink emblem -> low-ink garment screen-print variant (single ink, transparent surround).
WORDMARK-PLATE branch. Semantically select 'the abstract emblem symbol above the wordmark' on the on-ground brand-tuned raster — the INVERSE selection of step 10.

Mask-polarity trick #2 (the mirror of step 11): flat-fill the SELECTED EMBLEM with the ground colour to ERASE it, leaving only the SOLENE lettering on the ground. Same tool, opposite polarity — not a repeated identical call.
Knock the ground to transparency so only the lettering remains, letter counters (O, E holes) kept open.

Whole-image overlay tints the isolated lettering to one ink, counters preserved transparent. Report the ink chosen (may match the emblem plate for a one-ink brand kit, or a second ink — the agent's decision, stated in the note).
Tight bound around the one-ink wordmark for the plate.

Trace the single-ink lettering raster to a clean one-colour SVG spot plate. solene_brand_spec_note.txt is then authored from the agent's applied-settings log (the three correction deltas it dialled on the two photos and the export, plus the two plate inks it chose) — no connector call, no delegated typography pick, no reported/read colour value.

chaining_note: Strict output->input chaining with a genuine dependency graph, not a fan-out of one recipe. The palette is RECOVERED first: neutralise ref_wall(2) and ref_flyer(3) to their grey cards — two different corrections — and their agreement defines the true brand colour. That recovered truth then drives the master prep chain on the flat export: straighten(4)->crop(5)->cast-correct(6, a third distinct correction)->HSL brand-tune(7). flat_brandtuned(7) is the deliberate branch point (still on its off-white ground): the master forks to remove_background(8)->vectorize(9); the EMBLEM plate forks to select wordmark(10)->fill-erase wordmark(11)->remove ground(12)->one-ink overlay(13)->crop(14)->vectorize(15), with halftone(16) tapping the one-ink emblem; the WORDMARK plate is the mirror polarity — select emblem(17)->fill-erase emblem(18)->remove ground(19)->one-ink overlay(20)->crop(21)->vectorize(22). No step reuses a raw input except where legitimate (the three source assets each seed exactly one chain); every other step consumes a prior output. The two fill_area calls are opposite polarities and the two color_overlay calls act on different isolated subjects, so no call is an identical repeat.
difficulty_rationale: Long-horizon and depth-driven: 22 dependent connector calls, 11 distinct Adobe tools, across the tonal/colour family (image_apply_adjustments, image_adjust_hsl), the selection/mask family (image_select_by_prompt, image_fill_area), background/transparency (image_remove_background), single-ink treatment (image_apply_color_overlay), effect (image_apply_halftone) and vector (image_vectorize). Difficulty is NOT step count: strip the single upload and what remains is a three-stage reasoning problem — (1) recover an UNKNOWN palette by per-image white-balance to in-frame grey cards under opposite casts, (2) propagate that recovered truth as a third distinct correction onto a differently-cast flat export, (3) separate a single lockup into emblem-only and wordmark-only spot plates via mirror-image mask polarity while preserving interior negative space. Every step is headless [C]; there is NO generative step — no text-to-image, no gen-fill/expand, no upscale, no compositing, no canvas extension, no coordinate layout, no from-scratch art, and vectorize is only ever fed a prepared raster, never a selection. The agent must also correctly REFUSE the brief's literal 'redraw the concept' framing (unavailable) and instead do the production-and-separation work the connector can honestly deliver.
hardness_rationale: Failure gate (a CRAFT DECISION with a visible failure mode, never a self-measured loop): the two reference photos carry in-frame grey cards and were shot under OPPOSITE casts (warm wall, cool flyer), and the brief does NOT state which way to correct either — so the visible-failure path is copying one photo's correction to the other (or forcing one blanket white balance), which leaves at least one card obviously tinted and makes the two shots disagree on the emblem colour. The agent must neutralise each shot on its own BY EYE until both cards look clean neutral and the two shots visibly agree; it never reads a pixel and never reports a recovered hex — it reports only the temperature/tint/exposure it dialled. The mirror mask-polarity emblem/wordmark plate separation and the prep-before-trace chain are the other real gates: get the polarity backwards (fill the emblem instead of the wordmark, or feed a raw selection to vectorize) and the plate comes back a solid black blob with the interior gap filled. Human-hard elements (three, exceeding the two required): (1) cross-asset colour consistency to a common target — neutralise two differently-lit shots by eye via their grey cards and reconcile them into one recovered palette, a per-frame divergent correction that a single global move cannot satisfy; (2) constraint-reasoning around tool limitations — mask-polarity separation (fill the OTHER element flat to erase it, then vectorize what remains), knowing image_fill_area is right for ERASING but wrong for the plate itself (it fills interior negative space) while whole-image image_apply_color_overlay is right for one-inking an already-isolated subject, plus prep-before-trace discipline; (3) triage — the flat export is the trace source (after correction) while the two photos are colour references only and must never be traced. Deliberate trap: trusting the supplied flat export's baked-in (cast) colours instead of the grey-card-recovered look, and/or applying identical white balance to both differently-lit references — both look reasonable and both fail the grader's grey-card check; a secondary trap is feeding a SELECTION to image_vectorize (returns a black silhouette) or using image_fill_area to build the plate (fills the emblem's interior gap into a solid blob). Acceptance (grader-checked, on the output — the agent performs none of these measurements): each grey card reads neutral within tolerance and the two shots share one white point; the master and plates carry the recovered look, not the dull cast; each spot plate is exactly one ink with interior negative space kept open; the master shows no residual off-white halo (proof it was traced from the transparency-cleaned raster). The agent's own deliverable is an applied-settings log: the three correction deltas it dialled and the two plate inks it chose in solene_brand_spec_note.txt — no reported/read colour value.
